sections.html:
Next door to Florence County, Darlington County has the town of Darlington as its seat and Hartsville as its biggest community. It covers 560.59 square miles of land. Population slipped 8.4% between 2010 and 2020, ending at 62,905, and the latest estimate of 62,888 shows it holding steady. Manufacturing leads local jobs at 18.9%, with Sonoco and Duke Energy Progress among the major employers.

Tax business happens in the town of Darlington, even for a house in Hartsville. Plan your errands around that, since all three tax offices share one building.

The courthouse square address, 1 Public Square, Darlington, SC 29532, houses all three tax offices. Valuation is the Assessor's job, current payments go to the Treasurer, and delinquent accounts belong to the Tax Collector.

  • Treasurer: Room 203, phone 843-398-4160, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., closed on holidays.
  • Tax Collector: Room 207, phone 843-398-4170, same hours.
  • Assessor: Room 309, phone 843-398-4180. The county main line is (843) 398-4100.

For a current bill you can pay at the counter, use the drive-thru near the courthouse (8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.), go online through the Tax Search, View and Pay portal, or visit a local bank with your tax notice in hand. Branches in Darlington, Lamar and Hartsville take payments. A check should carry the receipt number.

Unpaid tax passes to the Tax Collector on March 17, along with a 15% penalty and added costs. The penalty builds in stages under the statute: 3% after January 15, another 7% by February 2 and another 5% by March 17 (S.C. Code 12-45-180).

Fees pile on top of the penalty in three installments.

DateCost added
March 17$20
July 1$40
September 1$60

Together the fees reach $120. One more rule catches people out: the office will not accept a current-year payment until older delinquent tax is cleared, so you cannot pay this year's bill and leave a prior year open.

The December tax sale is held in the Darlington Middle School gymnasium at 150 Pinedale Drive, and bidding opens at 10 a.m. The exact date comes from the Tax Collector at 843-398-4170. The Darlington News and Press carries ads for real property and mobile homes three weeks in a row beforehand.

For the 2026 sale, bidders must finish online registration by December 1, 2026 and pay a $10 nonrefundable fee. Bidder numbers are handed out Saturday, December 5, 2026 at the gymnasium.

  • The owner's last chance to pay a parcel's delinquent tax is 5:00 p.m. the day before; nothing is accepted on sale day.
  • Winning bidders pay in full by 5:00 p.m. the same day, with cash, a cashier's check or a money order.
  • Failing to pay a winning bid brings a $500 fine.
  • Bidders buy at their own risk, because a tax deed is no warranty deed.

Owners keep the right to redeem for 12 months after the sale under S.C. Code 12-51-90. Interest runs from 3% to 12% of the bid, rising the longer they wait. The Tax Collector can give you the final day for a specific parcel.

Every five years the Assessor inspects property under a revaluation plan that the SC Department of Revenue has approved. New construction, renovation or an appraisal review may trigger a visit earlier.

A home occupied by its owner is assessed at 4%, and other property at 6%. To earn the lower ratio, submit a legal residence application after your deed or bond for title is recorded and you move in. Any day before the January 15 penalty date will do. Losing eligibility must be reported within six months. If it is not, the penalty is 100% of the tax paid plus 0.5% interest per month, never less than $30 and never more than that year's tax.

Whoever owns the property on December 31 is named on the bill, and a buyer becomes responsible once a sale becomes final after that date. If you dispute a value, send the Assessor a written objection within 90 days of the mailed notice (S.C. Code 12-60-2510). The county offers a protest of valuation form, and the Assessor at 843-398-4180 can explain the Board of Assessment and Appeals and what comes next.

Owing back tax does not rule out a sale. Your title company will usually pay the balance from the proceeds. Ask the Tax Collector to write out the payoff, because the $20, $40 and $60 steps arrive on set dates and the total moves during the year.

Waiting for the tax sale calendar is risky. Parcels are advertised for three weeks, and the deadline to pay is 5:00 p.m. the day before the auction. If the auction has already happened, the redemption period still lets the owner pay, and a winning bidder does not gain a vested interest right away.

  1. Collect a written payoff from the Tax Collector.
  2. Clear any older delinquent year first, since the office wants it settled before current payments.
  3. Confirm your 4% status with the Assessor.
  4. Warn the title company if a sale date is close.

A cash sale can be timed to close ahead of the auction and does not wait on a buyer's lender, which matters when the last payment day is the afternoon before bidding.

Darlington sellers do best when they gather records before calling. Bring the tax notice, the receipt number from your last payment and, if you recently bought, proof of the recording date of your deed or bond for title. Those details let the Treasurer and the Tax Collector find your account fast, and they let the Assessor tell you whether a legal residence application is already on file.

If you inherited the house or are selling for a relative, ask each office what proof of authority it wants. A short call to 843-398-4100, the county main line, can point you to the right room in the building. Ask whether copies are fine or originals are needed, and whether the office prefers a visit or a mailed form. Write down the name of anyone who gives you a figure, with the date, so your closing office can follow up.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Darlington County property tax?
faqs.a: Go to the Treasurer in Room 203 at 1 Public Square, Darlington, or use the drive-thru, the online portal or a participating bank. The Treasurer's phone is 843-398-4160. Late bills go to 843-398-4170.

faqs.q: What is the penalty when Darlington County taxes are late?
faqs.a: A 15% penalty is added when taxes turn delinquent on March 17, plus $20 in costs. More costs follow: $40 on July 1 and $60 on September 1, for $120 total.

faqs.q: When is the Darlington County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county sells in December. Bidding starts at 10 a.m. in the Darlington Middle School gymnasium on Pinedale Drive. The date is available at 843-398-4170, and bidder numbers for 2026 are issued Saturday, December 5.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem after a Darlington tax sale?
faqs.a: State law allows 12 months, and interest of 3% to 12% of the bid applies depending on timing. The Tax Collector can confirm your parcel's last day.

faqs.q: How do I get the 4% rate in Darlington County?
faqs.a: Apply through the Assessor, with a legal residence application filed ahead of January 15. Homes the owner lives in qualify, and all other property is assessed at 6%. Report a loss of eligibility within six months.
